Define the term "contingency planning". [2]
items.answer: Planning in advance for possible future events or crises, so the business can respond quickly
items.markingKey: [2] for a full, accurate definition: planning in advance for possible future events or crises, so the business can respond quickly. [1] for a partial definition. Examples alone are not credited.

items.stem: Distinguish between crisis management and contingency planning.
items.answer: Contingency planning prepares for possible crises in advance; crisis management is the response while the crisis is happening.
items.markingKey: Contingency planning prepares for possible crises in advance; crisis management is the response while the crisis is happening. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why contingency planning can reduce the costs of a crisis.
items.answer: Pre-agreed actions, responsibilities and resources allow a quick response, limiting disruption, financial losses and reputational damage.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Pre-agreed actions, responsibilities and resources allow a quick response, limiting disruption, financial losses and reputational damage. (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A food manufacturer discovers that a batch of products may be contaminated. Outline the steps of an effective crisis response.
items.answer: Recall affected products immediately; inform customers and regulators transparently; set up a helpline; investigate the cause; fix the process; communicate updates; review the contingency plan afterwards.
items.markingKey: Recall affected products immediately; inform customers and regulators transparently; set up a helpline; investigate the cause; fix the process; communicate updates; review the contingency plan afterwards.

items.stem: Briefly describe the Tylenol recall and explain what it reveals about crisis management.
items.answer: In 1982 Johnson & Johnson recalled about 31 million bottles of Tylenol after seven deaths from tampered capsules, and relaunched with tamper-proof packaging. Putting customer safety first and communicating openly protected the brand
items.markingKey: Context (In 1982 Johnson & Johnson recalled about 31 million bottles of Tylenol after seven deaths from tampered capsules, and relaunched with tamper-proof packaging.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Putting customer safety first and communicating openly protected the brand – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to crisis management.

items.stem: "Contingency planning is a waste of resources because crises are unpredictable." Discuss.

items.answer: effective crisis management

items.answer: incremental innovation
items.markingKey: D. This is the definition of incremental innovation.

items.stem: Under the EU's GDPR, a firm can be fined up to:
items.answer: 4% of global annual revenue (or €20 m, whichever is higher)

Read the extract.

In 1982 Johnson & Johnson recalled about 31 million bottles of Tylenol after seven deaths from tampered capsules, and relaunched with tamper-proof packaging.

Explain why speed of response matters in a crisis. Refer to the extract or to another organization you have studied. [4]
items.answer: Social media spreads news immediately, so slow or unclear responses allow rumours and anger to grow, worsening damage.

items.stem: Explain why intellectual property protection encourages innovation.
items.answer: Patents and copyright let firms earn returns from their inventions without immediate copying, so they are willing to invest in costly R&D.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Patents and copyright let firms earn returns from their inventions without immediate copying, so they are willing to invest in costly R&D. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem:
Read the extract.

Tesco's Clubcard, launched in 1995, collects shopping data from millions of customers to personalise offers and plan stock.

Explain why management information systems improve decision-making. Refer to the extract or to another organization you have studied. [4]
items.answer: They give managers accurate, timely and relevant information, so decisions are based on evidence rather than guesswork.
items.markingKey: They give managers accurate, timely and relevant information, so decisions are based on evidence rather than guesswork. [1] for each relevant point identified and [1] for each point explained and applied to the case (2 × 2). Generic answers without application: maximum [2].

items.stem: Distinguish between contingency planning and crisis management.
items.answer: Contingency planning prepares for possible crises in advance; crisis management is the response while the crisis is happening.
items.markingKey: Contingency planning prepares for possible crises in advance; crisis management is the response while the crisis is happening. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Distinguish between product innovation and process innovation.
items.answer: Product innovation creates new or improved goods and services for customers; process innovation improves how products are made or delivered, often cutting costs.
items.markingKey: Product innovation creates new or improved goods and services for customers; process innovation improves how products are made or delivered, often cutting costs. items.stem: Briefly explain why AI raises ethical issues for businesses.
items.answer: AI may make biased decisions, replace jobs, misuse personal data and be hard to explain, raising questions of fairness and accountability.

In July 2024 a faulty CrowdStrike software update crashed about 8.5 million Windows computers, grounding flights and disrupting hospitals worldwide.

Using the extract, analyse how the 2024 CrowdStrike outage illustrates contingency planning. [4]
items.answer: Organizations with back-up systems and recovery plans restored services faster
items.markingKey: Organizations with back-up systems and recovery plans restored services faster [1]-[2]: relevant points with limited use of the extract; [3]-[4]: clear analysis explicitly linked to the extract.

items.stem: A firm had revenue of $800 m and spent $30 m on research and development (R&D). Next year revenue is $960 m and R&D spending $37.50 m. Calculate R&D spending as a percentage of revenue (R&D intensity) in each year and comment on the change.
items.answer: Year 1: 30/800 × 100 = 3.8%; year 2: 37.5/960 × 100 = 3.9%. R&D intensity has risen, suggesting a focus on innovation, though returns are uncertain and profit may fall in the short run.
items.markingKey: R&D / revenue × 100 for each year. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for both percentages. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [1] comment.

items.stem: Jonas writes: "More data always leads to better decisions." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Data must be accurate, relevant and well analysed; too much data can cause information overload and false patterns.
items.markingKey: Data must be accurate, relevant and well analysed; too much data can cause information overload and false patterns. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.
